summary: Ride Photos API (Emergent Object Storage) fully verified. All 10 pytest cases pass covering the full CRUD + auth/ownership contract: (1) /api/workouts/summarize with 40 samples returns a ride id; (2) POST photo returns ok+photo with path prefix 'roujaune/uploads/'; (3) list contains uploaded photo; (4a/b/c) proxy GET returns 200 image/png with Bearer AND with ?token=, and 401 without any token; (5) ownership enforced — foreign user prefix returns 403; (6) DELETE returns ok and list is empty afterwards; guards: text/plain rejected with 400 and unknown ride returns 404. Frontend regression clean: demo login works, /connections renders (Strava card + BLE demo device-btn-* -> ble-panel + ble-scan visible), no red-screen or crash introduced by RidePhotos import or the editable Strava note component in summary.tsx.
critical_code_review_comments: ride_photos.py: content-type derivation from client-supplied UploadFile.content_type is trusted for the extension mapping — acceptable given size cap + storage prefix isolation but consider server-side magic-byte sniffing for defense in depth.

ride-photos.ts: listRidePhotos / uploadRidePhoto / deleteRidePhoto use fetch without an Authorization header — this works because the AuthMiddleware also accepts session cookies/token via other paths, but sending Bearer token explicitly (like other API clients) would be more consistent.
seed_data_creation: Created and cleaned up a TEST_ ride via /api/workouts/summarize plus one PNG upload/delete cycle. Non-cleaned artifact: the ride_history document itself remains (no delete endpoint exercised), and one bad-request/404 attempt made no persistent state.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Photo storage integration is live and stable. Reuse /app/backend/tests/test_iter106_ride_photos.py as regression. Note: the ridePhotoUri() function on the frontend uses ?token= query to authenticate reads (AuthMiddleware supports this).
